1. Introduction 
1.1 Purpose 
The purpose of this Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document is to define the 
complete set of functional and non-functional requirements for the "Smart Traffic Management 
System for Urban Congestion" (Problem Statement ID - 25050). This SRS covers the entire 
scope of the proposed system, which consists of an AI-driven video analytics engine, a real-time

System for Urban Congestion" (Problem Statement ID - 25050). This SRS covers the entire 
scope of the proposed system, which consists of an AI-driven video analytics engine, a real-time 
signal optimization module, an incident dispatch system, and a comprehensive interactive web 
application dashboard. This document will serve as the primary reference for the development, 
testing, and evaluation teams throughout the software development lifecycle leading up to the 
Smart India Hackathon 2025 grand finale.

This document adheres strictly to the IEEE standard template for Software Requirements 
Specifications. The following typographical conventions and standardizations are used:

identifier (e.g., REQ-FEAT1-001) and an implicit priority level (High, Medium, Low)

1.4 Product Scope 
Current urban traffic management suffers from severe inefficiencies primarily due to fixed-timing 
signals, lack of intelligent oversight, and an inability to dynamically re-route traffic based on

Current urban traffic management suffers from severe inefficiencies primarily due to fixed-timing 
signals, lack of intelligent oversight, and an inability to dynamically re-route traffic based on 
real-time conditions. This leads to massive economic losses due to delays, high environmental 
impact (pollution and carbon emissions), and poor visibility for authorities during accidents or 
sudden congestions. 
The "Smart Traffic Management System" developed by Team Bitfusion-I is an advanced, 
interactive web application integrated with edge-based Machine Learning. Its primary purpose is 
to demonstrably reduce the average commute time by a target of $\ge 10\%$ in simulation 
environments (utilizing simulators like SUMO or CityFlow). 
Key Objectives and Benefits: 
● Continuous Real-Time Analysis: Incorporating CCTV feeds via OpenCV to extract 
traffic density parameters. 
● Intelligent Signal Optimization: Eliminating inflexible light schedules by dynamically

● Continuous Real-Time Analysis: Incorporating CCTV feeds via OpenCV to extract 
traffic density parameters. 
● Intelligent Signal Optimization: Eliminating inflexible light schedules by dynamically 
adjusting green and red phases using Deep Learning and analytical algorithms. 
● Rapid Incident Response: Automatically detecting anomalies (e.g., stationary vehicles) 
to dispatch traffic police via an SOS module, preventing congestion build-up. 
● Environmental & Economic Impact: Lowering $CO_2$, $NO_x$, and PM2.5 
emissions by reducing vehicle idling times, and cutting down fuel wastage to ensure 
better supply chain reliability for freight. 
● Social Impact: Ensuring safer intersections, reducing commuter frustration, and 
enabling emergency green corridors for ambulances and fire trucks. 

The software aligns with the Smart City Mission and provides municipal bodies with a 
centralized, middleware-based control dashboard that can adapt to multiple vendor protocols

2. Overall Description 
2.1 Product Perspective 
The Smart Traffic Management System is a new, self-contained software solution designed to 
act as an intelligent middleware layer. It is not intended to replace the physical hardware of 
traffic lights or the CCTV cameras themselves, but rather to act as the "brain" that connects 
passive monitoring devices with active control systems. 
System Context: 
● Inputs: Live RTSP/HTTP video streams from existing intersection CCTV cameras. 
● Processing Hub: A hybrid Edge-Cloud architecture. Heavy video processing 
(YOLOv5/OpenCV) occurs on edge devices or dedicated local servers to minimize 
latency and bandwidth. State management, analytics, and cross-intersection routing

(YOLOv5/OpenCV) occurs on edge devices or dedicated local servers to minimize 
latency and bandwidth. State management, analytics, and cross-intersection routing 
logic are handled by a cloud-based backend (Node.js/Express and Flask). 
● Outputs: Control signals dispatched via a Middleware API layer to local traffic 
controllers, and real-time visualization data sent to the React-based frontend dashboard 
via WebSockets (Socket.io). 
2.2 Product Functions 
The product encompasses the following major functional groups: 
● Video Ingestion & Feature Extraction: Capturing video frames and preprocessing 
them. 
● Object Detection & Vehicle Counting: Identifying cars, bikes, buses, and trucks, and 
tallying their numbers per lane. 

● Congestion Classification: Categorizing traffic density into Low, Medium, and High 
states. 
● Dynamic Signal Control: Calculating and dispatching optimal phase timings to 
intersections.

● Congestion Classification: Categorizing traffic density into Low, Medium, and High 
states. 
● Dynamic Signal Control: Calculating and dispatching optimal phase timings to 
intersections. 
● Incident Detection & SOS Dispatch: Identifying abnormal traffic flow, alerting 
authorities, and facilitating manual dispatch of field units. 
● Data Visualization & Analytics: Displaying live feeds, historical flow graphs, emission 
reduction statistics, and system health on a centralized dashboard.

2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints 
● Technological Constraints: The object detection pipeline must process frames rapidly 
enough to inform signal changes in real-time. This mandates the use of optimized 
models like YOLOv5 rather than heavier, slower alternatives. 
● Hardware Integration: The system must interface with legacy hardware. Since direct 
protocol access to old controllers might be restricted, the system must utilize a 
Middleware API layer and hard-coded constraints to ensure compatibility and safety. 
● Privacy & Regulatory Compliance: Under no circumstances will the system store

Middleware API layer and hard-coded constraints to ensure compatibility and safety. 
● Privacy & Regulatory Compliance: Under no circumstances will the system store 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Video feeds are processed in memory for 
vehicle counting; license plates and facial features are explicitly ignored to adhere to 
data privacy norms. 
● Network Reliability: Real-time optimization heavily relies on continuous video feeds. 
The system must degrade gracefully to fixed-timing (default hardware schedule) if the 
network connection or camera feed drops. 
● Financial Constraints: To ensure feasibility and scalability for municipal deployment, 
the solution must utilize open-source technologies (React, OpenCV, Flask) and avoid 
expensive proprietary software licenses where possible.

4.2 Real-Time Signal Optimization & Dynamic Re-routing 
4.1.1 Description and Priority 
Priority: High. This feature utilizes the data gathered from the video analysis to make intelligent 
decisions about traffic light phase durations, aiming to minimize queue lengths and waiting 
times. 
Benefit: 9 | Penalty: 8 | Cost: 5 | Risk: 8 
4.1.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences 
1. The ML service continually updates the lane density data (e.g., Lane A: 45 vehicles, 
Lane B: 10 vehicles). 
2. The optimization algorithm (e.g., Max Pressure Control) evaluates the current state. 
3. The algorithm determines that Lane A requires a longer green phase to clear the 
buildup. 
4. The system sends a control command to the Middleware API. 
5. The traffic signal hardware adjusts its timing schedule accordingly. 
6. Commute time decreases, preventing traffic spillover into adjacent intersections.

5. Other Nonfunctional Requirements 
5.1 Performance Requirements 
● Latency: Video processing and inference must occur with a latency of no more than 100 
milliseconds per frame to ensure real-time accuracy. 
● Throughput: The backend must be capable of handling concurrent data streams from at 
least 10 simulated intersections simultaneously without degradation in UI 
responsiveness.

● Throughput: The backend must be capable of handling concurrent data streams from at 
least 10 simulated intersections simultaneously without degradation in UI 
responsiveness. 
● UI Responsiveness: Real-time updates pushed via WebSockets must reflect on the 
React dashboard within 500 milliseconds of the event occurring in the backend. 
● Target Metric: The deployed optimization algorithms must demonstrate a simulated 
reduction in average commute time of $\ge 10\%$ compared to fixed-timing baselines. 

5.2 Safety Requirements 
● Conflict Monitoring: The system must implement hard-coded, hardware-level 
constraints to absolutely prevent conflicting traffic streams from receiving a Green signal 
simultaneously, regardless of ML model outputs. 
● Failsafe Reversion: In the event of an API failure, camera malfunction, or ML service 
crash, the system must immediately and automatically relinquish control back to the local

● Failsafe Reversion: In the event of an API failure, camera malfunction, or ML service 
crash, the system must immediately and automatically relinquish control back to the local 
controller's default fixed-timing schedule to prevent traffic gridlock. 
● Pedestrian Safety: Minimum green times and pedestrian clearance intervals must be 
strictly enforced and cannot be overridden by the dynamic optimization algorithm. 
5.3 Security Requirements 
● Data Privacy: The system shall not capture, record, or store any high-resolution imagery 
capable of identifying individuals or vehicle license plates. All data stored must be strictly 
aggregated numeric counts. 
● Authentication & Authorization: Access to the Control Dashboard must be secured 
using robust authentication. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) must be enforced to 
ensure only authorized administrators can trigger manual overrides or alter intersection 
configurations.

● Data in Transit: All communications between the frontend, backend, and external APIs 
must be encrypted using TLS/HTTPS and secure WebSocket (WSS) protocols. 
5.4 Software Quality Attributes 
● Robustness: The architecture must handle erroneous inputs gracefully (e.g., a camera 
lens being obscured by rain/dirt) by detecting low-confidence inferences and falling back 
to safe timing schedules. 
● Interoperability: The use of a Middleware API layer ensures that the system is highly 
interoperable, capable of integrating with hardware from multiple different vendors 
without rewriting core logic. 
● Scalability: The containerized nature of the Node.js and Flask microservices allows for 
easy horizontal scaling across cloud providers as the number of monitored intersections 
grows.

● Scalability: The containerized nature of the Node.js and Flask microservices allows for 
easy horizontal scaling across cloud providers as the number of monitored intersections 
grows. 
● Usability: The frontend design (via Figma/Tailwind) prioritizes a clean, intuitive layout 
with high contrast, minimizing the cognitive load on traffic operators. 
5.5 Business Rules 
● Emergency Preemption Rule: If an authorized operator initiates an "Emergency Green 
Corridor" for an SOS dispatch, all dynamic optimization rules are suspended for that 
route until the override is manually lifted. 
● Public Transport Priority Rule: Buses detected in the traffic flow are assigned a higher 
weight multiplier in the congestion calculation, ensuring mass transit is cleared through 
intersections faster than private vehicles. 

● Data Retention Rule: Aggregated traffic flow data should be retained indefinitely for 
long-term urban planning analytics, while raw incident logs should be archived after 90

● Data Retention Rule: Aggregated traffic flow data should be retained indefinitely for 
long-term urban planning analytics, while raw incident logs should be archived after 90 
days. 
6. Other Requirements 
6.1 Environmental Impact Tracking 
The system shall include an algorithmic module that correlates the reduction in vehicle idling 
time (derived from improved flow metrics) to estimated reductions in greenhouse gases. This 
module will calculate and display: 
● Estimated fuel wastage prevented (in liters/gallons). 
● Estimated reduction in $CO_2$ emissions. 
● Estimated reduction in $NO_x$ and PM2.5 emissions, contributing to cleaner urban air 
and supporting the Environmental co-benefits outlined in the project presentation.
